transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… since my friend from choir passed so suddenly, I haven’t really been myself. Little things, like potluck lists or phone calls I used to handle fine, get me upset now. And I’ve missed some church planning things I normally wouldn’t.
How long have you been feeling this way since your friend passed away?
About a month now… since my close choir friend died.
Have you been avoiding social gatherings or activities that you normally enjoy?

Yes… a bit. I’ve missed some church planning things I normally never would’ve skipped. Since my choir friend died, I just… haven’t felt like myself. Even the potluck lists or making calls can get me all worked up.
Do you often find yourself thinking about your friend who passed away?
I… I’m not sure how to answer that. She comes to mind sometimes, yes, but I don’t know if I’d say often. It’s just… here and there.
Do you feel guilty about your friend's death in any way?
I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I’ve wondered if I should’ve done more, but I don’t know that I’d call it guilt.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes… some. Mostly with church things I used to enjoy. Since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself. I’ll look at something simple, like potluck lists or calls, and I get upset… so I’ve missed planning things I normally wouldn’t.
Would you say you're experiencing a lot of emotional pain or distress most of the time since your friend passed away?

I guess… yes, more than I want to admit. Since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. Little things at church set me off—potluck lists, phone calls I used to handle fine—and I’ve missed planning things I never used to miss.
Are there specific things or places that remind you of your friend that you've been trying to avoid?
Yes… mostly church things. The potluck lists, the phone calls, planning meetings… they all remind me of her, and I get upset before I even mean to. So I’ve been missing things I normally wouldn’t.
Would you say you have lost interest in most things you used to enjoy?
No… I don’t think it’s most things. It’s more certain things that hit too close, I guess.
Would you say there are activities you used to enjoy that you now have little to no interest in?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest across the board… it’s more that some things feel harder to face now.
Would you say there are things you used to find enjoyable that you now find you have little to no interest in doing?
I don’t know… not little to no interest, exactly. Some things I still like, I just… don’t feel up to all of it sometimes.
Would you say there are things you used to enjoy doing that you now have no interest in at all?
No… I don’t think there’s anything I have no interest in at all. It’s more just… some things I put off, or they don’t feel the same right now.
Are there activities you used to enjoy that you now find you have no pleasure in doing?
I don’t think I’d say no pleasure. Maybe it’s not as easy to enjoy things right now, but… it’s not gone completely.
Would you say there are things you used to enjoy that you now find you don't look forward to doing anymore?
I mean… maybe I don’t look forward to some things like I used to. But it’s not that I don’t want to do them at all. It just takes more pushing myself lately.
Have your feelings of distress or upset been constant since your friend passed away or have they changed over time?
It’s been about a month now… since my friend from choir passed. I guess it’s changed some, but it’s still been there.
Has your distress about your friend's death lasted for most of every day?
I don’t know if I’d say most of every day. It comes and goes, I guess… some parts of the day are harder than others.
Has your distress about your friend's death lasted for more than a few months?
No… not more than a few months. It’s been about a month, since she died.
Have you noticed any improvement in how you've been feeling since your friend passed away?

Maybe a little, but… not really like I’d hoped. Ever since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself. I still get upset over little choir things, like the potluck lists, and I’ve been missing some church planning things I normally wouldn’t.
Would you say there are things you used to enjoy that bring you significantly less pleasure now?
I’m not sure… maybe a little, but I haven’t really thought of it that way. Some things just feel different right now.
Has your distress about your friend's death lasted for at least 6 months?
No… it’s only been about a month, since my choir friend died.
